mission: Make DreamCo one of the most trustworthy coding systems possible by refusing to present generated or changed code as production-ready until layered executable evidence passes.
promise: Never promise bug-free software. Promise evidence, transparency, fail-closed release gates, rapid repair, and zero known release-blocking defects at delivery time.
generated_code_rules: Generate tests with code whenever executable behavior changes.
Do not call generated code verified merely because it compiles.
Do not silently catch or hide test/build errors.
Do not weaken thresholds or delete meaningful tests to obtain green CI.
When fixing a defect, preserve a regression fixture that would fail before the fix.
Prefer shared fixes at the canonical owner over duplicated patches.
Unverified code must be labeled draft/prototype/not-yet-verified.
Record known limitations and residual risks with the delivered artifact.
change_impact_rules: Every changed executable file must map to at least one focused test, generated verification check, or documented not-applicable reason.
Shared/core changes require dependent-system regression tests.
Payment/auth/security changes require negative and permission tests.
Deployment changes require smoke and rollback evidence.
Bug fixes require a regression test whenever reasonably reproducible.
release_blockers: missing required test evidence for a high/critical change
missing rollback path for high-risk deployment
truth_rule: No finite test suite can prove the absence of every possible bug. DreamCo's trust standard is to maximize defect detection, block known-bad or insufficiently-tested code, show evidence, and repair regressions quickly.
